lara.title: The Step Below
lara.text:
Lara finds you on the back steps after close. The lantern beside you is guttering. She sits down one step below yours, with her knees together and her hands folded in her lap. She used to sit like that outside the office on Alder Street, when one of you was waiting to be told something.

She tells you how she got here, in a low, careful voice. She followed a rumor about a stranger in a grey hood through three provinces. She slept in stables, and in chapels when they'd let her. She cleaned for her meals. The black coat got shabbier with every road.

"I asked in every town. People thought I was simple." She smooths her skirt over her knees. "I couldn't stay anywhere you weren't, Sam. I tried it for about a week, in a place with a kind landlady. I know that isn't healthy. I do know."

She's looking at your shoes. Her dark lipstick is chewed at one corner.
ngpp: She's smoothing her frayed sleeve when she stops and looks at the lantern wick. Then at the step under her, and at your boots. "That's odd," she says quietly. "I feel as if I've sat here before. In exactly this spot." She goes back to her sleeve and does not mention it again.

"Alder Street feels like it was lifetimes ago, Sam," she says. "So why does sitting one step below you feel like something my body already knows?" She presses her knees together. "Like muscle memory from another world. I'm sorry. That sounds strange."

She doesn't take the lower step tonight. Lara sits beside you, close, and her fingers lace into your sleeve. "I don't know how many back steps we've shared," she says. "Some of them aren't in my memory. But I knew where you'd be, and I'm sure of it."

choices.label: "I'm really glad you found me."
choices.res: "I'm really glad you found me," you say. She lets out a long, shaky breath, as if she's been holding it since Alder Street. A moth circles the lantern, and she watches it instead of crying, which for Lara is the same thing. After a while she moves up one step, so her shoulder touches your knee.

choices.label: "You're allowed a life of your own, Lara."
choices.res: "You're allowed a life of your own, Lara." She nods slowly, as though it's a lesson she'll need to learn more than once. She doesn't leave, but she looks out at the dark street instead of at you, and you can almost hear her turning the idea over, one careful page at a time. "I'll think about it," she says. "I mean that."

image.comp: sitting one step below him on a back staircase at night, hands folded in her lap, looking up at him with dark kohl-lined eyes
image.setting: back steps of a lantern-lit inn at night

lara.title: Can't Sleep
lara.text:
Lara can't sleep. She never could. At midnight she decides the washroom needs fresh towels, takes a stack up, and opens the door.

You're in the tub.

She stops in the doorway with her arms full of linen. Then she lifts the whole stack until it hides everything below her eyes. Her lace cuffs are trembling. Steam curls around the hem of her black dress.

"I'm so sorry. I'm so sorry. I didn't think anyone would be up. I'm just going to stand here."

She doesn't move.

A drip falls from the tap. It's as loud as a clock.

Over the top of the towels, her eyes are very wide and lined in black. They're fixed on a point on the wall some way above your head. She's holding them there by will. As you watch, the towels creep a little higher.

1.title: Warm Towels, Warm Hands
1.text:
At midnight Lara taps on the washroom door and waits before she comes in. She's carrying one towel, warm from the kitchen stove. She walks up to the tub with it and doesn't hide behind it.

The steam has curled the loose hair at her throat. She kneels down beside the cedar rim and turns back her lace cuffs, one fold at a time.

"I had the dream again," she says quietly. "The corridor one, where all the doors are shut." Her hands aren't steady. "May I wash your back? Only until I stop shaking. It helps to have something to do, and it helps that it's you."

choices.label: Let her—then dry her cold hands between yours and kiss her
choices.res: You let her stay. She starts on your back with the cloth, and her cool fingertips warm against your wet shoulders until the trembling stops. You take her hands, dry them between yours and turn to face her. She sighs, her cheeks dark, and leans into your chest. "That's better," she says. Her mouth is a hand's width from yours.
choices.fallbackRes: Her quiet hands trace careful circles across your back until the shivers leave her shoulders. She doesn't say anything. After a while she rests her cheek against your arm, and her breathing slows with the steam. "Thank you," she whispers. "I think the corridor is shorter when it's you." She stays there until the water goes cool.

choices.label: Wrap her in the warm towel and sit with her on the bench
choices.res: You wrap her in the warm towel and sit with her on the bench. She tucks her knees inside the linen and goes quiet. "The doors in the dream are all shut," she says. Then, after a long time, "Not in this one." Her head drifts onto your shoulder, and she's half asleep before the lamp burns down.

image.comp: kneeling beside the cedar rim turning back her lace cuffs, holding one warm towel, unsteady hands, vulnerable searching look

3.title: No Nightmares Tonight
3.text:
You hear bare feet on the boards at midnight. Lara comes into the steam with no towels to hide behind.

She unbuttons her black dress at the stool and lets it fall. She unclasps the choker last. Then she steps into the hot water, naked, and sits down across from you with her knees between yours. Her dark hair floats out around her shoulders.

She finds your hand under the surface and brings it up to rest on her bare breast, over her heart.

"No nightmares tonight, Sam," she says. "I decided. I want you to hold me, and then I want you inside me, and I'd like you to stay until morning."

choices.label: Draw her gently onto your lap in the warm water
choices.res: She unbuttons her dress and steps in without a towel, and her hair floats out around her shoulders. She takes your hand under the water and puts it on her breast, over her heart. It's racing. "I'm not frightened," she says. "I just want it to be you." Then she slides onto your lap, her arms around your neck, and kisses you.

choices.label: Hold her against your chest and touch her gently beneath the mist
choices.res: She tucks her cold toes between yours under the water. You pull her against your chest, one hand on her back and the other low on her hip. She shivers, and it isn't from the cold. "Keep going," she whispers, with her mouth against your throat. "Slowly, please." The steam curls around you both, and her breath is hot on your neck.

image.comp: sitting naked in the hot water across from him, knees between his, dark hair floating, guiding his hand to her bare breast, soft determined gaze

choices.label: Laugh and ask her to leave the towels
choices.res: You laugh and ask her to leave the towels. She sets them down with enormous, ceremonial care, backs out of the room with her eyes on the ceiling, and shuts the door. In the empty hall you hear her laugh once, short and surprised, as if she'd forgotten she could. She's still smiling when you pass her in the morning.

choices.label: "Stay and talk, if you can't sleep."
choices.res: "Stay and talk, if you can't sleep." She sits on the edge of the tub with her back to you and tells you about the night noises of the Alder Street orphanage. The pipes, the coughing, the matron's keys. By the end she's leaning against the wood, nearly asleep, her voice gone soft and slow. You don't say much. You don't have to.

choices.label: Send her to bed
choices.res: "Go to bed, Lara." "Of course." She goes at once, silent as a cat, with the towels still in her arms. You don't hear the stairs. In the morning she apologizes four times, and the fourth is to the towel rack. She doesn't look at you when she does it, but she's left the warm one on your chair.

image.comp: frozen in a washroom doorway, arms full of folded towels hiding most of her face, mortified

lara.title: A Lamp in the Window
lara.text:
Whenever you're out in the evening, there's a lamp lit in the courtyard window when you come back. It took you a while to notice, and a while longer to work out who was lighting it.

Tonight you're very late. A supplier kept you, and a cold fog has come down over Hollowmere. You can hardly find the gate.

The lamp is there. It's a small yellow blur in the grey.

Lara is sitting under it in her black shawl. She has a book open on her knee. From the way the pages lie, she hasn't turned one in hours. Moths are drifting around the glass.

She stands up when she sees you. Then she doesn't know what to do with her hands, and she folds them, and unfolds them.

"I wasn't waiting," she says. "I was keeping it warm. Someone ought to. It's a horrible thing, coming home to a dark window. I did it for years."

choices.label: Take her upstairs out of the fog and warm her up properly
choices.res: You wrap your hoodie around her cold shoulders and guide her upstairs. The fog stays out. Once the door shuts, Lara pulls you toward the bed with both hands on your chest, shivering, her black shawl slipping to the floor. "I'm still cold," she says. It's the closest she's ever come to a lie, and you both know it.

choices.label: Sit with her
choices.res: You share the bench and the shawl, which smells of lavender and old paper. The moths circle the lamp. She leans against your shoulder and, for once, doesn't ask whether you're tired of her. After a while she closes the book and sets it on the stones. "I'll keep it lit," she says. "If you'll sit here with me for a bit."

choices.label: "Come out with me next time."
choices.res: "Come out with me next time." She says "maybe," very softly, and tugs the shawl closer around her. It's better than the "no" she'd have given last month, and you both know it. She looks at the lamp for a while, then at the gate. "I'd need something black," she says. "Something with pockets."

image.comp: sitting under a courtyard lamp in a black shawl with a book, looking up as he returns
image.setting: lantern-lit courtyard at night, moths around the light

lara.title: Don't Go
lara.text:
The house needs you in the capital. A supplier is in dispute and it has to be settled in person. It will take three days, with a night on the road each way.

Lara hears you say so in the corridor. She has a stack of folded sheets in her arms, and she goes as white as they are.

She follows you to your room. She stops at the door and takes hold of the frame, so hard that her knuckles lose their color.

"Everyone who says they'll come back." Her voice is flat and careful. "The woman who was going to adopt me said Tuesday. The first family said after the holidays. You said you'd call me on your birthday, and then there was a truck." She shakes her head. "It isn't your fault. None of it is anyone's fault. I just know how this goes, Sam. I know."

Her eyes are enormous and completely dry.

She doesn't cry, and that's worse.
ngpp: She stops with her hand on the key, in the doorframe. Her breath catches. "Odd," she says, in the careful voice she uses when she's frightened. "It's as though I've pressed this into your palm before. Warm from my fist." She shakes her head, then doesn't take the key back.

"Why does some part of me insist that you always came back?" she whispers, still gripping the frame. "I've no reason to think so, Sam. Everybody else didn't." She looks at you as if you're a locked door she suddenly knows the key to. "I'm trying not to trust it. It won't go."

She breathes out, shaking, and lays her room key on your palm before the fear can take over. "I remember Alder Street," she says. "And some deeper piece of me remembers trusting you to bring this back. I can't prove it. But I do." Her fingers close yours around it, firmly.

choices.label: "I'll never leave you."
choices.res: "I'll never leave you." It's what she wants to hear. It isn't quite true, and both of you know it. She nods and holds on a little too tightly when you hug her, her fingers digging into your coat. She doesn't say a word about it. The three days are very long, and she's at the gate at dawn on the fourth.

choices.label: "I can't promise forever. I promise I'll come back."
choices.res: You tell her you can't promise forever, but that you'll come back. She cries, but it's a different kind, the kind that loosens something. She presses her room key into your palm, warm from her fist. "So you have to return it," she whispers. You put it inside your shirt, and she watches you do it.

choices.label: Hand her the linen schedule to run while you're gone
choices.res: You give her the linen schedule and the house keys. She runs the house for three days with ledgers and lists and not a single crooked pillow. When you return she meets you at the door, proud in a way that has nothing to do with you, and that is exactly the point. "It was fine," she says. "I was fine. I'd like to do it again."

image.comp: gripping a doorframe with both hands, pale, dark eyes wide, ponytail swinging

lara.title: Midnight Garden
lara.text:
Lara asks if you'd come to the courtyard at midnight. She asks it formally, in advance, as though she has thought hard about whether she's allowed.

She takes you to the far corner behind the rain barrels, where nothing has ever grown.

There's a garden there now. It's a few feet square. She has planted it with white flowers that hold a faint glow in the dark, like spilled milk. There are little paths laid out in pebbles. There's a watering can with her initials scratched into the handle.

"The seeds were in the market. The woman said they only open at night." She crouches and turns one flower toward you. "I thought, well. So do I."

She stands up and puts her hands behind her back.

"It's mine. I made it on my own, in the hours when everyone's asleep. I didn't make it for you, and I'd have made it if you weren't here." She says it as if she's testing whether it will hold. "I'd like you to see it, though."

choices.label: Tell her it's beautiful, and mean it
choices.res: She laughs, shaky and surprised, and tucks a glowing blossom behind your ear. "Now you're in the garden too," she says. The flowers hold their faint light around you both, and the pebble paths show white. She doesn't look away this time. For a long moment she just looks at you, in the half-dark, as though she's learning your face.

choices.label: Plant the next row together
choices.res: She teaches you to space the seeds with two fingers' width between them. You do it wrong, over and over, and she lets you, because it's your row now. She kneels beside it in the dirt in her good black dress and fixes nothing. When you finish she says, "It'll come up crooked." She sounds very pleased.

image.comp: kneeling in a patch of glowing white night flowers, offering a small blossom up to him, shy smile
image.setting: moonlit courtyard garden of pale night-blooming flowers

lara.title: Being Left
lara.text:
Lara asks you up to the roof on a clear night. She stands at the edge with her hands wrapped in her shawl. She has clearly practiced what she wants to say, and she says it slowly, choosing each word.

"I used to think loving someone meant they'd never leave. So I held on to people as hard as I could. It never kept anyone."

The wind lifts her ponytail.

"I think it's closer to this. Being able to be left, and still being me afterward. I couldn't do that when I got here. I think I can now. You went to the capital for three days, and I watered my garden, and I was all right." Her voice steadies as she goes. "So I'm not saying this because I'm frightened. I want you because I choose you, Sam. Out of everyone, on purpose."

She kisses you.

Then, for the first time in her life, she's the one who takes your hand and leads you inside. The door closes behind you both.
ngpp: Her breath catches, as if another life already gave her this nerve. She stands at the roof's edge with the shawl wrapped around her and looks at the moons. "That's strange," she says. "I feel like I've said this, and meant it. I don't know when." She keeps going all the same.

"Alder Street taught me how doors close," she murmurs beside your cheek. "So why does walking through yours feel like keeping a promise I already kept?" She doesn't wait for an answer. She laces her fingers through yours and holds on, not tightly, and she's looking ahead the whole time.

"Let the cycles erase whatever they like, Sam," Lara says against your lips, as she draws you inside. Her voice doesn't shake. "I choose you in this life, and in every one I can't remember. I know I've done it before. I'm certain. Don't tell me I haven't."
lara.goLead: In the quiet bedroom, Lara lets her black shawl fall from her bare shoulders. She lays both palms flat over your heart, and then she pulls you down onto the quilt.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Lara nods, and this time it doesn't look like a door closing. "I can wait," she says, steady. "I'll keep the lamp lit. Don't make it too long." She picks up her shawl, and at the top of the ladder she stops, turns back and kisses your cheek, quickly, then goes down before she can change her mind.
